  - l: 'And Hephaestus, when then the heart-paining word he heard,\nset out to go to the smithy, evil in his wits deep-devising,\nand set on the anvil-block a great anvil, and hammered bonds\nunbreakable, not to be undone, so that firmly on the spot they would stay.'
  - i: 'And when Hephaestus heard the word that pained his heart, he set out for the smithy, devising evil deep in his mind, and set a great anvil on its block, and hammered out bonds that could not be broken or undone, so that they would stay fast right there.'

Lines of the Odyssey count too (Homer shares formulae across the two poems): reuse their English unless the Iliad context forbids it, and say so in new-renderings.md when you depart. Where a whole unit of yours has the same Greek as a published Iliad unit, its `l` and `i` must be identical to the published ones (the validator enforces it). Where only a line inside your unit repeats, reuse the published wording for that line as far as your sentence allows.
